evidence: Juv. 6.455 (Lewis & Short): crūre tenus mediō tunicās
terms.comment: To pull a long tunic up through the belt so as to move freely; the participle succīnctus, girt up, is “ready for action”. Lewis & Short: mostly poetic and post-Augustan.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 399.
